To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
REG4 expression is associated with better survival in non-mucin producing colorectal cancer patients.
REG4 expression was an independent prognostic marker in non-mucinuous colorectal cancer.
REG4 is an independent marker of better prognosis in non-mucus CRC patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of REG4 in colorectal cancer and the impact of this expression on prognosis.
the identification of novel prognostic factors for CRC patients.
the prognostic significance of REG4 expression in colorectal cancer (CRC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
REG4 expression is not a prognostic biomarker for CRC patients in general, but that it might be a marker of good prognosis in non-muccinous CRC.
REG4 expression may be a marker of favorable outcome, but only in non-mucin producing tumors.
REG4 expression is a favorable prognostic marker for non-mucinous colorectal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

REG4 ICH expression in non-mucin producing colorectal cancer is associated with better prognosis and that REG4 expression correlates with the intestinal differentiation markers MUC2, 4, and 5AC in colorectal cancer.
REG4 ICH expression in non-mucin producing tumors is a favorable prognostic marker for CRC.
REG4 expression in the tumor is a marker of better prognosis in non-muccinous colorectal cancer, but not in mucinous colorectal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prognostic value of REG4 expression is dependent on the histological type of cancer.
REG4 expression may help in identifying patients with non-mucinous tumors who may not benefit from adjuvent therapy.
REG4 ICH expression is a novel independent biomarker of favorable prognosis in CRC.
